articles.title: A Memorable Rainy Night
articles.content:
Last New Year's Eve, I broke the code.

This summer, it sprouts again in the cache.

I thought I was a lost pointer,

drifting at the bottom of a C stack,

tossing in assembly registers, unable to sleep.

Then I opened last year's search history

and found that unfinished blog.

Like a letter never sent,

it waited in the stack of time.

Turns out passion was never a detour.

It was the way home.

Sixteen, the pointer hung

between school and what I love.

Tonight it lands.

You say HTML is your land,

but I see those lit screens at night

already answered the choices for you.

Those nights talking to machines,

those evenings debugging the same lines,

were not stolen time.

They were practice.

Practice for saying yourself clearly in this world.

No need to ask how passion meets the future.

When you wrote your first line of poetry,

the future moved aside.

Tonight the clock hands meet.

Past and future blur.

That blog that missed last New Year's Eve

is now, on an ordinary summer morning,

your gift to yourself.

Go study for the exam, Observer.

C and assembly stay.

Your blog stays.

They wait in some corner of GitHub,

like a promise that does not expire.

Next year, you come back better,

to finish the code you started

and read the books you put down.

By then, you'll know:

Every wrong turn was a shortcut to yourself.
